items.title: Section: A New Ground Opens — Eighteen Obstacles to Concentration

items.zh: 如是已說有尋有伺等三地決擇。三摩呬多地決擇，我今當說。謂補特伽羅，多隨煩惱染污相續，不能正證心一境性。云何名為多隨煩惱？謂有諂、誑、矯、詐、無慚無愧、不信、懈怠、忘念、不定、惡慧、慢緩、猥雜、趣向前行、捨遠離軛、於所學處不甚恭敬、不顧沙門、唯悕活命不為涅槃而求出家。
items.en: Thus I have already explained the decisive discernment of the three grounds with investigation and reflection, and so on. I shall now explain the decisive discernment of the Ground of Meditative Equipoise. A being whose mind-stream is repeatedly defiled by many secondary afflictions cannot rightly realise single-pointedness of mind. What are the many secondary afflictions? Flattery, deceit, pretence, deception, shamelessness and lack of a sense of disgrace, faithlessness, laziness, forgetfulness, lack of concentration, wrong wisdom, dullness, promiscuous mixing, pressing eagerly forward, casting off the yoke of freedom from company, insufficient reverence for the training rules, disregard for renunciant life, and seeking ordination only to survive rather than for the sake of nirvana.

items.title: Section: Flattery, Deceit, and the Face Saved Through Evasion

items.zh: 云何有諂？謂自有過，而不能於大師、智者同梵行所，如實發露。云何有誑？謂不真實顯己功德。彼實無德，而欲令他諸有智者同梵行等了知有德。云何有矯？謂於增上戒毀犯尸羅，或於軌範毀犯軌範。由見聞疑，他所舉時，遂用餘事假託餘事，或設外言而相誘引，如經廣說。謂由諂、誑增上力故。
items.en: What is flattery? Having faults oneself, yet unable to confess them truthfully before the Teacher, the wise, or one's fellow practitioners of pure conduct. What is deceit? Falsely displaying one's own virtues, when one actually has none, wishing the wise and one's fellow practitioners to know one as virtuous. What is pretence? Transgressing the precepts of higher discipline, or breaching the rules of proper conduct, and when accused by another through what was seen, heard, or suspected, thereupon using some other matter or pretext, or offering deflecting words to draw the questioner away, as extensively explained in the sutras. This arises through the enhancing power of flattery and deceit together.

items.title: Section: Deception Born of Fear, and Six More Ways the Mind Resists Stillness

items.zh: 云何有詐？謂怖他故，或復於彼有所悕故，雖有犯重而不發露，亦不現行。非實意樂，詐於有智同梵行所，現行親愛、恭敬、耎善身語二業。云何無慚無愧？謂觀於自、或復觀他，無所羞恥。故思毀犯，犯已不能如法出離，好為種種鬪調違諍。云何不信？謂於佛法僧心不清淨，於苦集滅道生不順解。云何懈怠？謂執睡眠、偃臥為樂，晝夜唐捐，捨眾善品。云何忘念？謂於久遠所作、所說，不能隨念，不令隨憶，不守根門，不正知住。云何不定？謂於定地，下至作意亦不能得。云何惡慧？謂住自見取，執不平等，難捨言論。云何慢緩？謂不捷利，亦不明了。不自起舉，無所能為。不能以身供侍有智同梵行者。
items.en: What is deception? Out of fear of others, or out of hope for something from them, not confessing even a grave transgression, nor again committing grave evil deeds. Without genuine sincerity, feigning affection, respect, and gentle bodily and verbal conduct before wise fellow practitioners. What is shamelessness towards self and other? Feeling no disgrace when regarding oneself or another, deliberately transgressing, and once having transgressed, unable to make amends as the Dharma prescribes, given to quarrels and disputes. What is faithlessness? An impure heart towards the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, not accepting the truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path in accordance with reality. What is laziness? Clinging to sleep and reclining as pleasure, squandering day and night, abandoning wholesome practices. What is forgetfulness? Unable to recall what was long ago done or said, not guarding the sense faculties, lacking clear awareness. What is lack of concentration? Unable to attain even the most preliminary right application of mind towards the grounds of concentration. What is wrong wisdom? Holding to one's own view, clinging to an unequal account of causation, finding such discourse hard to relinquish. What is dullness? Neither sharp nor clear, unable to rouse oneself, incapable of accomplishment, unable to serve wise fellow practitioners even with one's own body.

items.title: Section: Mixing Freely, Pressing Forward, Refusing the Yoke of Solitude

items.zh: 云何猥雜？謂樂與在家及出家眾共相雜住。又樂尋思諸惡不善欲尋思等，乃至家勢相應尋思，多隨尋思、多隨伺察。云何趣向前行？謂受僧祇、或復別人諸衣服等所有利養，或請僧祇及與別人，皆名趣向。若諸苾芻，於如是事最初前行，故名趣向前行。云何捨遠離軛？謂於遠離邊際臥具、遠離眾惡人所習近似寂靜室，遠棄捨之，不生欲樂。
items.en: Foolish sluggishness in action is called unsharp. A mind without pure faith is called unclear. Being bound up with laziness is called failing to rise above. What is promiscuous mixing? Delighting in mixing and dwelling together with both householders and renunciants. Also delighting in dwelling on unwholesome thoughts of desire and the rest, up through thoughts bound up with family standing, repeatedly indulging and scrutinising them. What is pressing eagerly forward? Receiving robes and other requisites, whether belonging to the sangha or to individual monks, or being invited with the sangha or individually, and, among monks, always being first to come forward for such things, is called pressing eagerly forward. What is casting off the yoke of solitude? Being unwilling towards austere bedding at the margin of comfort, or a quiet dwelling remote from bad company, abandoning and refusing any wish for it.

items.title: Section: The Final Three — Precepts, Renunciant Life, and Why One Ordains at All

items.zh: 云何於諸學處不甚恭敬？謂遭厄難，寧捨學處，不棄身命。志求身樂及與壽命，不能隨護所有學處。云何不顧沙門？謂棄捨學處，好為退轉。或犯尸羅，行諸惡法，於內腐爛，廣說乃至實非梵行自稱梵行，況當悕求沙門果證八支聖道。云何唯悕活命不為涅槃而求出家？謂或為王之所逼迫而求出家。或為怨賊之所逼迫、或為債主之所逼切、或為恐怖之所逼切、或為財寶常所匱乏恐畏不活而求出家。不為自調、自靜、自般涅槃而求出家。
items.en: What is insufficient reverence towards the training rules? When meeting hardship, choosing to abandon the training rules rather than give up body or life, seeking bodily ease and longevity, unable to guard the training rules one has received. What is disregard for renunciant life? Abandoning the training rules, readily falling back, transgressing precepts, committing unwholesome deeds while rotten within, up to falsely claiming pure conduct one does not have, let alone hoping to realise the fruits of renunciant life through the noble eightfold path. What is seeking ordination merely to survive rather than for nirvana? Seeking ordination because compelled by a king, pursued by an enemy or bandit, pressed by a creditor, driven by fear, or afraid of not surviving due to constant poverty, not for the sake of taming oneself, stilling oneself, and realising one's own nirvana.

items.title: Section: Sorting Eighteen Afflictions by Their Root

items.zh: 當知此中，依同梵行而共止住有所違犯，發起最初四隨煩惱。依增上戒有所違犯，當知發起無慚無愧。依增上心及增上慧，當知發起始從不信，乃至惡慧諸隨煩惱。此中不信及與懈怠，依俱違犯；忘念、散亂，依增上心違犯而起；惡慧，依犯增上慧起。不信、懈怠增上力故，當知發起慢緩、猥雜、趣向前行、捨遠離軛。忘念、亂心及與惡慧增上力故，當知發起於諸學處不甚恭敬、不顧沙門、唯悕活命不為涅槃而求出家。
items.en: One should know that, depending on transgressions committed while dwelling together with fellow practitioners of pure conduct, the first four secondary afflictions arise. Depending on transgression of the higher training in precepts, shamelessness arises. Depending on the higher training in mind and the higher training in wisdom, the afflictions from faithlessness through wrong wisdom arise. Among these, faithlessness and laziness depend on transgressing both; forgetfulness and distraction arise depending on transgressing the higher training in mind; wrong wisdom arises depending on transgressing the higher training in wisdom. Through the enhancing power of faithlessness and laziness, dullness, promiscuous mixing, pressing eagerly forward, and casting off the yoke of solitude arise. Through the enhancing power of forgetfulness, a scattered mind, and wrong wisdom, insufficient reverence towards the training rules, disregard for renunciant life, and seeking ordination merely to survive arise.

blocks.text: Fascicle 62 ascertains the Stage of Concentration. It begins with an honest list of eighteen things that block meditation, most of them about honesty and community life.

Master Cháng Bǎi: many secondary afflictions stain body and mind and so obstruct meditation. With flattery, when a fault is raised one grows angry and cannot confess; with impure precepts, meditation cannot arise.
Flattery hides one's faults; deceit displays virtue one lacks; pretence deflects an accusation by talking about something else; deception feigns affection.

Master Cháng Bǎi: one fears others will learn of the fault, or hopes for respect and gain from them. With no conscience towards oneself and no shame towards others, one breaks precepts on purpose. Some cling to sleep, wasting day and night. Some cannot give up assertions, not seeing that speech is merely designation.
Master Cháng Bǎi: wanting offerings, this person always walks first. Unable to bear the yoke of solitude, one cannot leave unwholesome situations.
Master Cháng Bǎi: in hardship such a person would rather give up the precepts than body and life. Some were compelled to go forth, not to tame, still, and free themselves.
Shamelessness depends on the higher precepts; faithlessness and wrong wisdom on the higher mind and wisdom; forgetfulness and distraction on the higher mind.
Most of the eighteen obstacles are failures of honesty. The treatise suggests that meditation begins not on the cushion but in being truthful with others.

quiz.q: Which being cannot rightly realise single-pointedness of mind?
options: one who has not yet taken full ordination and joined the Sangha
one who has not yet met a good friend or heard the true Dharma
one whose mind-stream is repeatedly defiled by many secondary afflictions
one who still lives at home enjoying desires and has not gone forth
quiz.why: The treatise opens the Ground of Meditative Equipoise with this obstacle. Master Cháng Bǎi: many secondary afflictions stain body and mind and so obstruct meditation, keeping one from worldly and transcendent single-pointedness.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain why secondary afflictions make meditation hard to attain?
options: all are seeds of root afflictions, so one must first reach a noble fruit before meditating, as the text requires
accused of a fault one grows angry and cannot confess, and impure precepts make meditation hard
they cost one's monastic status and the right to dwell together
they make the body ill, so that one cannot sit for long
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi traces a chain: with flattery and the like, when a fault is raised one grows angry, cannot confess and be purified, and with impure precepts meditation is hard to attain. The obstacle runs through precepts to meditation.

quiz.q: 猥雜 is rendered "coarseness." Going by the lecture, where should the emphasis lie?
options: on rude manners, which is what the text explains, so §4's wording is the inaccurate one
on laziness, so it belongs with the preceding item, dullness
on pride, so it should be rendered "arrogance"
on mixing, as §4's own "mixing and dwelling together" shows
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 猥雜 has two kinds, a mixing within the mind and a mixing in outward life. §4's explanation agrees with him, speaking of dwelling together and of indulging in thoughts. The label alone would mislead readers.

quiz.q: What does one with 有矯 do when accused? How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe it?
options: one talks about something else to escape the matter of the transgression
one confesses at once but insincerely, mouth and heart differing
one turns and accuses the other, and they dispute
one stays silent and waits for the Sangha to decide
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one uses the method of talking about something else to escape the matter. Because of flattery one cannot confess truly, and borrows other words so that others will not know of the fault, fearing the loss of gain.

quiz.q: What are the two motives behind 有詐, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: to win people over, a bodhisattva's skilful show of affection, not a secondary affliction
fearing that others will know the fault, or hoping for respect and gain from them
craving pleasures or hating fellow practitioners
lacking faith in the Jewels or in karma
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one fears others will learn of the fault, or hopes to receive respect and gain from them. These two motives lie behind the feigned affection the treatise goes on to describe, so the outward kindness is not sincere.

quiz.q: 亦不現行 is rendered "nor letting it show." What is at issue, per 《披尋記》 and the lecture?
options: none: it just means hiding the fault, a repeat of 不發露, as the lecture has it, so nothing is lost
不現行 should be "dormant"
it leaves out 犯重, the grave transgression
it means not committing such grave deeds, whereas the English has hiding them
quiz.why: The 《披尋記》 reads this as no longer committing grave evil. The concealment is already in "not confessing," and the feigning comes in the next sentence, so "nor letting it show" adds a third point of hiding instead of the sense of restraint.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define laziness?
options: clinging to sleep and reclining as pleasure, squandering day and night, abandoning wholesome practices
unable to recall what was long ago done or said, not guarding the faculties, without clear awareness
an impure heart towards the Three Jewels
unable to attain even an application of mind towards concentration
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: clinging to sleep and lying down as pleasure, wasting day and night, and abandoning good practices such as calm and insight. The other options describe forgetfulness, faithlessness, and lack of concentration, listed nearby.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 難捨言論 under wrong wisdom?
options: a gifted debater hard to persuade, a habit of talking too much
being reluctant to leave the place of teaching
being reluctant to set aside the texts one has studied
not knowing that speech is mere conceptual designation and its objects unreal, one cannot let go of it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one does not understand that speech is by nature merely designated and that its objects are not real, and so cannot give up such assertions. The treatise places this alongside holding to one's own view.

quiz.q: This is rendered "whether communal or offered by a private donor." Is 別人 right?
options: yes: 別人 means a donor outside the Sangha, so the phrase fits, as the lecture divides it
no: 別人 should be "laypeople"
no: 別人 is the individual monk as opposed to the Sangha, and the invitation clause is also missing
no: 僧祇 should be "monastery"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with desire for offerings, this person always walks first. The lecture says lay people invite the assembly or individual monks, so 別人 is a monk, not a donor. The clause on invitations is left out too.

quiz.q: When meeting hardship, what does one without reverence for the training rules do?
options: one would rather lose one's life than the rules, the rules being the root of liberation
one asks the Sangha for an exemption
one would rather give up the training rules than give up body or life
one leaves the Sangha for a time and takes the precepts again later
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in hardship one would rather give up the precepts received than give up body and life. Training rules, he adds, are precepts, the classes of monastic rules that must be studied. Option B describes the opposite, a reverent person.

quiz.q: Which is not among the cases of seeking ordination merely to survive?
options: being compelled by a king or pursued by an enemy or bandit
being pressed by a creditor or driven by fear
being in constant poverty and afraid of not surviving
going forth to tame and still oneself and realise nirvana
quiz.why: The treatise lists five compulsions and ends by saying such people do not go forth to tame, still, and release themselves. Master Cháng Bǎi: taming means taming afflictions, and stilling means stillness among the sufferings of birth, ageing, and death.

quiz.q: Depending on what transgression does shamelessness arise?
options: on transgression of the higher training in precepts
on both the higher mind and wisdom, as with the whole group from faithlessness on
on dwelling with fellow practitioners
on receiving gain and offerings
quiz.why: The treatise is explicit: shamelessness depends on the higher precepts. Faithlessness through wrong wisdom depends on the higher mind and wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi adds that the two named next depend on both, confirming this division.
